name: The Pool Room
summary: An original all-3D New York dive-bar scene that ends with a physics-solved pool break.
tagline: We built a bar that doesn’t exist. Then broke a rack in it.
lead: A thirty-second cinematic film moves through an invented bar before a billiards break closes the scene.

sections.heading: Built from scratch
paragraphs: The room, props, lighting, and shots were created for this original showroom build. It is not a real bar or a client space.
The scene is designed to show how a concept can feel tangible before a physical location or shoot exists.

sections.heading: A room with a point of view
paragraphs: The visual system uses a dive-bar setting to make material, light, sound, and motion part of one authored moment.
It is a Lab experiment, not evidence of client work or a real-world outcome.

disclaimer: Lab showroom build. Not a client space, client result, or real-world promise.
interactionNotes: The official page presents a cinematic opening sequence and a pool-break film.
Fifteen official opening-frame WebP images are exposed in the page HTML.

name: Six-Story Walk-Up
summary: An illustrative New York corner rendered as one living 3D asset for real estate, games, and cinema.
lead: Orbit, tilt, and zoom through an invented walk-up to explore a place before a photo shoot or physical build exists.

sections.heading: Explore the whole corner
paragraphs: The walkthrough uses a single interactive 3D environment rather than a fixed image.
It is an illustrative capability build for thinking about place, not a client result.

disclaimer: Lab showroom build. People, places, numbers, and business states are illustrative unless the page states otherwise; this is not a client result or a promise.
interactionNotes: Drag sideways to orbit, drag vertically to tilt, and pinch or scroll to zoom.
The direct HTML requires JavaScript to show the model and exposes no static representative image.

name: Neon District
summary: An illustrative night district built as an interactive city scene with people, cabs, beacons, and changing moments.
tagline: A living city that remembers you.
lead: Explore an invented district by orbiting the scene and activating parts of the city.

sections.heading: A city you can touch
paragraphs: Beacons, citizens, and cabs invite interaction while a guided tour moves through the scene.
Time-of-day and event controls change the illustrative environment without making a business-performance claim.

disclaimer: Lab showroom build. People, places, numbers, and business states are illustrative unless the page states otherwise; this is not a client result or a promise.
interactionNotes: Tap beacons, citizens, and cabs; drag to orbit; pinch to zoom; use the on-page tour and time controls.
The direct HTML requires JavaScript to show the model and exposes no static representative image.

name: Scroll Into Motion
summary: A scroll-controlled visual study that places sixteen New York moments inside one frame.
tagline: Sixteen real New York moments inside one frame.
lead: The visitor controls the edit: move forward, drag back, or stop on any frame.

sections.heading: Scroll is the editor
paragraphs: The study is built around direct control instead of autoplay: the scene changes only when the visitor moves it.
It demonstrates a motion approach for launch films, lookbooks, campaigns, and brand stories.

disclaimer: Lab showroom build. This motion study is not a client result or a promise.
interactionNotes: Scroll forward, pull back, or pause at any moment; the sequence does not autoplay.
The direct HTML exposes no static representative image; its visual sequence is loaded through the interactive build.

name: Micro-Animations
summary: Seven interaction studies inside an illustrative ordering interface, each showing how small feedback can clarify an action.
lead: Press, throw, hold, undo, slide, flip, and commit through short interactions designed to make an interface easier to read.

sections.heading: Feedback carries the action
paragraphs: The studies focus on button acknowledgement, sheets, destructive holds, undo, tabs, theme changes, and form completion.
The ordering interface is illustrative; it is a place to test motion behavior, not a real order flow or client result.

disclaimer: Lab showroom build. The interface is illustrative and not a client result or a promise.
interactionNotes: The official study maps each interaction to a small behavior: press-down acknowledgement, sheet throw, hold-to-confirm, undo toast, sliding tabs, light/dark flip, and error/success feedback.
The direct HTML exposes no static representative image.

name: AHA Laser Poster
summary: A responsive poster experiment with a laser-drawn wordmark and a pull-chain interaction.
lead: A typographic poster uses a simple physical gesture to trigger its visual response.

sections.heading: Poster as interaction
paragraphs: This is a responsive design demo centered on a laser-drawn wordmark and one pull-chain gesture.
Its AHA name is separate from the After Hours Agenda client/product case study; it is a Lab poster experiment.

disclaimer: Lab showroom build and design demo, not a client result or a promise. Do not merge with the After Hours Agenda case study.
interactionNotes: Use the pull-chain control to trigger the poster behavior.
The direct HTML exposes no static representative image.

name: Studio Engine
summary: An illustrative business-direction generator that turns a rough idea into a sample creative direction.
lead: Choose an illustrative business type and aesthetic direction to explore how a small tool can move an early idea forward.

sections.heading: Start with a direction
paragraphs: The project uses sample business types and visual directions to demonstrate an interactive starting point.
It is not a real client site or client result.

disclaimer: Lab showroom build. The business choices and outputs are illustrative; this is not a real client site, client result, or promise.
interactionNotes: Select a sample business type and visual direction to drive the illustrative experience.
The direct HTML exposes no static representative image.

name: Growth Street
summary: An invented flower-shop story that uses interactive visual props to explain a possible path from attention to orders.
tagline: A systems story, not a performance report.
lead: The fictional shop and its people, orders, reviews, and money visuals make an abstract growth system easier to inspect.

sections.heading: A model for explanation
paragraphs: The flower-shop narrative is invented to show relationships among discovery, action, and follow-through.
Dots, tickets, crowd scenes, reviews, and money are explanatory props, not reported traffic, sales, reviews, or revenue.

disclaimer: Lab showroom build. The flower shop is invented; shown people, orders, money, and outcomes are illustrative and are not performance data or a promise.
interactionNotes: The page uses interactive story props to explain the system. Do not present them as metrics.
The direct HTML exposes no static representative image.

name: Goliath
summary: A Little Fight brand experiment that uses ten scroll-controlled street posters to carry one message.
lead: The scroll behaves like a projector, moving through an original campaign without photography or video.

sections.heading: One message, many frames
paragraphs: This is Little Fight’s own campaign study, built around a sequence of ten posters and a scroll-controlled projection effect.
It demonstrates how a clear idea can organize a campaign; it is not a client result.

disclaimer: Lab showroom build around Little Fight’s own message, not a client result or a promise.
interactionNotes: Use scroll as the projector that carries the poster sequence.
The direct HTML exposes no static representative image.
